messages:
acme_ops_john: Hey team — our production upload just aborted. UI and API show tenant credits = 0 in the middle of a run. We expect monthly refill at 2025-06-01T00:00:00Z. Can someone check? Account: acme-tenant-42.

maya_support: sorry to hear that, john. can you paste the response headers/any 429s you saw? roughly what time (UTC) did this happen?

acme_ops_john: Happened at 2025-05-31T23:59:30Z. We got 429s on some requests and the /quota endpoint returned headers below. curl output:```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-tenant-id: acme-tenant-42
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset: 1751236800
content-type: application/json```
Also attached a short server log line: `upload: chunk 237 failed -> 429`

maya_support: thanks. pinging billing + oncall. @eng_oncall_raj @billing_claire do you see any scheduled reset mismatch for this tenant?

eng_oncall_raj: taking a look. quick question — is the account set to local-midnight or UTC-midnight? the x-credits-reset header shows 1751236800 (which is 2025-06-01T02:00:00Z) — that looks odd vs expected 00:00Z.

billing_claire: checked the billing config for acme-tenant-42: billing window is UTC 00:00 by default. no custom timezone on the org. ledger shows a reset at 2025-06-01T00:00:00Z (1751236800 is actually 2025-06-01T00:00:00-02:00?). wait let me reformat timestamps and confirm.

infra_bot: automated note: edge-cache:quota-headers TTL=30s; quota-cache-invalidation events: none in window 2025-05-31T23:59:00Z->2025-06-01T00:01:00Z.

eng_oncall_raj: quick repro suggestion: can you call the /quota endpoint repeatedly for 90s and paste the headers? we want to see if API and UI disagree. also, are you using long-running websocket/streaming tokens for the upload? those can keep reserved counts until reconnect.

acme_ops_john: we're using parallel chunk uploads over HTTPS (no websocket). here's two subsequent /quota responses 20s apart:```# 2025-05-31T23:59:30Z
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset: 1751236800
# 2025-05-31T23:59:50Z
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset: 1751236800```
Then at 2025-06-01T00:00:05Z UI showed credits back to normal and uploads resumed.

maya_support: ok that pattern helps. sounds like the ledger did the reset at 00:00 but some edge caches were still serving stale headers for up to ~30s which caused clients to see 0 and/or get 429s. eng, can you confirm edge TTL behavior?

eng_oncall_raj: confirmed — our quota header cache on the CDN layer had a 30s TTL. in high-throughput uploads, clients hitting different edges could see stale zero for a few seconds after the ledger flip. the ledger itself completed the refill at 2025-06-01T00:00:00Z. inflight retries then cleared.

billing_claire: ledger audit shows refill wrote +monthly bucket at 2025-06-01T00:00:00Z successfully. there was no double-draw or missing topup.

maya_support: resolution summary for customer: the refill occurred on schedule (00:00Z). a short-edge-cache TTL (30s) caused some requests right around the boundary to observe pre-reset state and receive 429s. workaround: retry after 60s or enable client-side backoff/retry. we'll invalidate edge cache for your tenant now to be safe. sorry for the disruption. :heart:

acme_ops_john: thanks — we retried and all good. can you advise on best practice to avoid this during large uploads?

eng_oncall_raj: recommended: implement exponential backoff with jitter and keep retry window >=60s for monthly reset boundaries; optionally detect near-boundary (within ±30s) and delay heavy writes until after you see the refill header. we'll also lower the CDN TTL for quota headers to 5s in the next deploy to reduce this window.

billing_claire: filing a follow-up ticket to review edge-cache TTLs for quota headers and to add a monitor around reset-time 429 spikes for high-traffic tenants.

maya_support: closing this thread for now — reopen if the problem recurs. thanks for the quick repro steps, john.

acme_ops_john: appreciated, team. saved our deploy.
